text: Turbulence is just air moving at different speeds, like a boat crossing choppy water.
Rising heat, mountains, storms, and those fast jet streams all stir it up.
And your plane is built for it.
Airliners are designed to handle at least two and a half times the force of gravity.
Then engineers add a fifty percent safety margin on top.
In one famous test, engineers bent a Boeing seven-seven-seven's wings upward about seven meters before they finally snapped.
That's far beyond what turbulence should ever do.
Most turbulence injuries happen to people who aren't wearing a seatbelt.
So next time that seatbelt sign dings, buckle up.
